sentence: This project studies how small molecules, lipids, and protein regulators change how transmembrane receptors work.
This project studies a cell signaling pathway that is highly elevated in dystrophic skeletal muscles of Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
This project builds ways to track care coordination between primary care providers and specialist teams for patients with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias.
This project builds a device for growing airway epithelial cells in motion to study how motions of the airway affect cell biology.
This project provides tools that measure metabolic activity in cell culture, animal model, and clinical specimens relevant to diabetes and obesity.
This project studies how opioids used for cancer pain affect the anti-tumor immune response in head and neck cancer.
This project studies how mutations in a protein subunit of neurofilaments cause a hereditary nerve disease, using stem cells from patients and a mouse model.
This project studies how kinesins help cells control polarity during embryonic cell division in vertebrate development.
This project tries to find out how butyrate affects Clostridioides difficile and the infection it causes in the gut.
This project studies how drugs that target immune cells expand immunity in peripheral tissues but also cause toxicity against healthy tissues.
This project builds contrast agents that let diagnostic ultrasound show engineered immune cells deep in tissues, using anti-tumor macrophages as a model.
This project tests a device that uses electricity to deliver plasmid DNA for a combination cancer therapy in a melanoma model and in companion animals.
This project builds ways to manufacture cardiomyocytes from human pluripotent stem cells more reliably, using single cell molecular profiling to find failure points.
This project adds an automated organoid dispenser to a screening core to speed up studies of disease and therapy development.
This project studies the genetic changes that happen as cancer develops, including DNA damage tolerance pathways that lead to drug resistance.
This project covers cardiovascular epidemiology, including translational epidemiology, statistical genetics and computational biology.
This project tests whether an altered lighting schedule increases tumor formation in a mouse model of lung adenocarcinoma through a transcription factor.
This project provides analysis services that help design experiments and analyze data for clinical, laboratory and translational ovarian cancer research projects.
This project tries to find endogenous retroviruses whose expression and genetic variants are linked to myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome.
This project builds an imaging technology with a sensing collimator detector to detect ultralow photon fluxes in patients receiving alpha particle therapy.
